conversation.content:
Good morning—thank you for making time for this visit. My name is Maya Patel, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician here to check in on how you’re adjusting to new motherhood. I’ll be guiding you through a brief questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s simply a way for us to hear—confidentially—about your mood, anxiety, and well-being over the past week. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything we discuss stays between us unless you tell me otherwise. We’ll cover ten questions; most take just a minute each. Ready to begin?

1. In the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things, even during the little everyday moments?

[soft sigh, eyes a bit distant]

Honestly… not very often. Things that used to make me giggle—like my husband’s goofy jokes—just kind of bounce off me lately. I’ll try to smile for him, but it feels forced. Maybe once or twice the whole week I caught myself letting out a real laugh, and even then it faded fast.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

[shakes head slowly]

Not really… I mean, sometimes I can manage a little smile, but it feels like work. Most of the week I’ve just felt flat, like the joy is stuck behind a wall.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[shoulders sag]

Hardly at all. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it all feels like one more chore. A couple of times I thought “maybe I’ll enjoy this,” but the feeling disappears before I even start.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[eyes drop to hands, voice small]

Yeah… more often than I’d like to admit. If the baby won’t settle, I automatically think, “I’m doing something wrong; other moms know how to soothe their babies.” When I spilled pumped milk last night, I sat on the nursery floor crying because it felt like proof I’m failing him. I know logically it’s just an accident, but the “bad-mom” voice in my head jumps in every time.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

[wrings the edge of the hospital blanket]

Pretty much every day. Even when he’s napping I catch myself staring at the monitor, worried his breathing looks “off,” or I scroll through articles about SIDS and suddenly I’m convinced something awful is about to happen. There’s no real reason—I know he’s healthy—but the thoughts just race and I can’t shut them off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

[breath hitches]

A few times this week. It’s like a wave—my heart starts racing, I feel shaky, and suddenly I’m sure something terrible is about to happen, even though nothing’s wrong. It passes after a while, but in the moment I feel like I can’t catch my breath.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days. Between feeding every couple of hours, trying to sleep when I can, laundry, texts I forget to answer… it piles up. I’ll be rocking the baby and feel like I can’t keep my head above water. I manage the essentials, but it still feels like I’m drowning in small stuff.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

[lets out a slow breath]

Yeah… even when the baby’s finally down, I’ll lie there staring at the ceiling for an hour or more. My mind keeps looping through everything I think I messed up that day, or I picture scary “what-ifs” about him. I drift off eventually, but then I jolt awake at every tiny squeak from the crib. Most nights I’m awake two or three extra times, just stuck in that worried fog.
I have felt sad or miserable

[eyes well up]

A lot of the time. I wake up with this heavy feeling in my chest, like the day’s already lost before it starts. I’ll be feeding him and tears just start rolling—nothing specific happened, it’s just this gray sadness sitting on me.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[nods slowly, voice shaky]

Yeah… it’s happened three, maybe four times this week. Sometimes it’s when he won’t latch and I feel useless, other times it’s just quiet in the nursery and the tears start before I even know why. The littlest thing sets me off, and once I start it’s hard to stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[shakes head quickly, eyes widening]

No—never. I’ve felt overwhelmed and low, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel better so I can take care of my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: New mother, 1-week post-delivery  
Informant: Self  
Date: ___

Symptoms reported:
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness (daily crying spells)
- Marked loss of interest/enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities
- Excessive guilt / self-blame (“bad-mom” cognitions) over minor incidents
- Generalized anxiety, intrusive “what-if” fears, nocturnal hypervigilance
- Episodic panic sensations (racing heart, breathlessness) without identifiable trigger
- Sleep disruption beyond infant-care demands (initial insomnia, anxious rumination, frequent re-awakening)
- Feeling overwhelmed/drowning in routine tasks most days

Pattern: Symptoms present “most days” over the past week, interfere with basic functioning and infant-care confidence.

Risk flags:
✓ Meets core mood criteria for possible PPD  
✓ Co-occurring anxiety/panic symptoms  
✓ No current self-harm ideation (explicitly denied)

Safety: Denies suicidal or infanticidal thoughts; no self-harm plans.

Screening impression: High clinical likelihood of postpartum major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; warrants formal diagnostic evaluation and safety-planning.
